comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C8. Both evaluations find the pharmacological actin perturbation experiments well-supported, with peer reviewers explicitly praising the 'state-of-the-art optical recording' and 'well-executed genetic and pharmacological perturbations.'

Perfect agreement on claims C9-C15. Both evaluations support the genetic manipulation findings across multiple stimulation protocols. Peer reviewers highlight 'further mechanistic insight regarding the specific function of mDia1/3' as a major strength.

Perfect agreement on claims C16-C18. Both evaluations accept the IMM-01 gain-of-function experiments without critique, with peer reviewers noting the complementary approach strengthens conclusions about mDia function.

Perfect agreement on claims C19-C21. Both evaluations support the ultrastructural evidence, with peer reviewers explicitly affirming that EM analyses 'demonstrate the quantitative changes in numbers of synaptic vesicles and in uncoated membrane invaginations.'

Perfect agreement on claims C22-C24. Both evaluations support the structure-function analysis of mDia1 membrane localization. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the ΔN mutant experiments demonstrating membrane association is critical for function.
Perfect agreement on claims C25-C26. Both evaluations accept the STED super-resolution localization data without concerns, with peer reviewers praising the 'state-of-the-art' methods used throughout.

Perfect agreement on claims C27-C31. Both evaluations support the proteomic findings and interaction partner identification. Peer reviewers accept these data as contributing to understanding of 'presynaptic actin dynamics and synaptic vesicle endocytosis.'
Perfect agreement on claims C32-C35. Both evaluations accept the mDia1 accumulation upon dynamin inhibition without methodological concerns, supporting mDia1's involvement in endocytic processes.
Perfect agreement on claims C36-C38. Both evaluations support the F-actin visualization and accumulation findings upon endocytic blockade, with no concerns raised about quantification methods.

Perfect agreement on claims C39-C41. Both evaluations strongly support the K994A mutant experiments. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm that 'actin polymerization-defective mutant mDia1 (K994A) failed to restore delayed vGLUT1-pHluorin endocytosis.'

Perfect agreement on claims C42-C44. Both evaluations accept the jasplakinolide rescue experiments as critical evidence linking mDia function to actin regulation and endocytosis, with no concerns raised.

Perfect agreement on claims C45-C48. Both evaluations support the RhoA findings. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight 'new information regarding the control of both presynaptic actin dynamics and synaptic vesicle endocytosis via Rho/Rac cascades' as a major strength.

Perfect agreement on claims C49-C51. Both evaluations accept the Rac1 hyperactivation findings as part of the compensatory mechanism, with peer reviewers affirming the 'significant advance in knowledge, with particular respect to Rho/Rac signalling.'

Agreement on claims C52-C54 regarding Rac1 inhibition. Both evaluations acknowledge the statistical limitation of the additive effect while accepting the overall conclusion about Rac1's role in the synergistic relationship.

Perfect agreement on claim C68. Both evaluations strongly support this overarching conclusion about the interdependent signaling network. All peer reviewers explicitly affirm the substantial mechanistic advance and convincing evidence.
